findings.printedLatin: Haec pure facienda est: quia non est pars una peccatorum dicenda, et altera reticenda; neque levia confitenda, et gravia diffitenda.
findings.englishAsRendered: This must be made purely: because one part of one's sins is not to be told and another kept silent; nor light things confessed and grave ones denied.
findings.conjecture: The Latin negation governs the whole pair (non [una dicenda et altera reticenda]); English needs the scope carried explicitly, e.g. "because it is not the case that one part of one's sins should be told and another kept silent" or "because one part of one's sins is not to be told while another is kept silent".
findings.whyContradiction: As rendered, the clause most naturally reads as prescribing that one part is NOT to be told and another is to be kept silent — i.e. partial concealment — which is the opposite of its own governing sentence "Haec pure facienda est" / "This must be made purely," and of the immediately following "Nec alter accusandus et ipse excusandus" ("Nor is another to be accused and oneself excused"), the whole point of which is that nothing be held back.
